title: Organisation of preoperative anaemia pathways for elective hip and knee replacement: a scoping review
abstract: Objective: to map how preoperative anaemia pathways for elective hip and knee replacement are organised and how they reach patients who live far from the treating centre. Design: scoping review following JBI methods with PRISMA-ScR reporting. Results and conclusions will be written after charting.
introduction: Anaemia is common before joint replacement and often detected too late for treatment. Pathways differ in screening point, triggers and leadership, and reports rarely describe them in reproducible detail.
methods: Librarian-designed search including grey literature; dual screening; piloted charting form covering screening point, triggers, leadership, treatments and location, times, postponements, communication and access for distant patients; descriptive synthesis.
results: Not yet written. The section will present the flow of reports, frequency tables, a figure of times by screening point and a summary of provisions for distant patients.
discussion: The discussion will translate the charted options into design choices for the centre's pathway and state where evidence on organisation is missing.
limitations: Reliance on reports that may describe intended pathways; incomplete reporting of times.
conclusion: To be written after charting; it will not rank pathways by effectiveness.
summary: PRISMA-ScR structured draft with results left empty until charting.
